brief.capability: Map FITS primary/IMAGE header, data and padding byte ranges without loading arrays.
brief.pain: A rejected small FITS needs physical HDU boundaries and padding evidence before array interpretation.
brief.contract: 80-byte printable ASCII cards, complete 2880-byte blocks, ordered primary SIMPLE/BITPIX/NAXIS and consecutive NAXISn, IMAGE extensions with EXTEND=T and PCOUNT=0/GCOUNT=1. Dimensions0..4, axis sizes0..1000000, BITPIX8/16/32/64/-32/-64. END and space header padding are required. Nonzero data padding is an exit1 finding. Byte ranges use exclusive ends; no arrays are allocated.
brief.limits: 8 MiB,32 HDUs,144 cards per header. No tables, random groups, compressed extensions, pixel interpretation, scaling, WCS, repair or complete FITS conformance validation. CHECKSUM/DATASUM are explicitly unverified. Nonstructural card values are not semantically validated.
brief.acceptance: Correct two-HDU layout, zero dimensions, float64 data extent, quoted slash handling, malformed card order/duplicates, truncation and nonzero padding.
brief.notes: Astropy and CFITSIO already provide much broader FITS IO and verification; fitsio exposes CFITSIO-backed table/image access. Astroz is a terminal astronomy workflow. No missing HDU-inspection capability is claimed. The precise ranges and strict subset are our interface choice.
brief.overlap: No FITS HDU mapper was found among all198 owned repositories. Existing media inspectors do not implement astronomical block/card semantics.
brief.expected: Exit0: primary data is empty at byte2880; IMAGE data occupies bytes5760..5764 and padding ends at8640.

brief.capability: Explain ELF LOAD ranges, zero-fill and declared page-permission unions without executing a binary.
brief.user: Build and release engineers reviewing a small ELF handoff.
brief.pain: Individual segment flags do not explain shared-page permission unions or overlapping virtual mappings.
brief.contract: ELF32/64, little/big endian, identification/version1, EXEC/DYN, standard header/program-entry sizes and1..128 program headers. LOAD validates file/memory sizes, class address limits, known R/W/X flags and p_align congruence. Report backed/zero-fill intervals, overlap ambiguity, entry outside executable LOAD, W+X segments/stack and W+X page flag unions. Page-offset incongruence is a finding. Page size is a declared power of two512..65536, default4096; interval sweep avoids enumeration of huge virtual ranges. PT_INTERP is read as bounded ASCII but never opened/executed.
brief.limits: 8 MiB. Other program-header kinds are ignored, section headers/relocations/ABI-specific semantics unverified. No loader simulation, ASLR, dynamic linking, DWARF, exploitation assessment or safety certificate. Missing GNU_STACK is unknown information, not a healthy-stack claim. Page union is a declared model; actual OS loading/permissions can differ.
brief.acceptance: Both classes/endians, shared-page union, BSS, virtual overlap, entry failure, file/align rejection and huge virtual intervals without page allocation.
brief.notes: LIEF parses and modifies broad executable formats; pyelftools and Goblin already expose ELF segments/flags and much more. Our evidence report is a narrow read-only workflow, not proof of an absent feature or a safer parser.
brief.overlap: Filesystem POSIX ACL tooling and binary media tools do not model ELF virtual LOAD intervals. No owned ELF page-union inspector was found.
brief.expected: Exit1 intentionally: separate RX/RW LOAD byte ranges share a4096-byte page, whose declared flag union is RWX; zero-fill ranges remain explicit.

brief.capability: Map classic TIFF IFD metadata and grayscale strip ownership, including aliases and out-of-file evidence.
brief.user: Image ingestion maintainers investigating a small grayscale TIFF.
brief.pain: Offset/count arrays and inline fields can conceal metadata/strip collisions before pixel decoding.
brief.contract: Classic TIFF II/MM version42. At most32 acyclic word-aligned IFDs,128 fields per IFD; known field types1..12 have bounded payload extents and inline values up to4 bytes. Width/height, explicit8-bit samples, compression1, grayscale photometric0/1, one sample and contiguous planar layout. Explicit rows-per-strip and exact offset/count array sizes, including final partial strip. Expected raw bytes equal width times strip rows. Strip/strip and strip/metadata overlaps are exit1 findings with no winner policy; exact aliases remain visible.
brief.limits: 8 MiB, width/height/rows1..1000000,4096 decoded values per interpreted tag,4096 strips total, first256 overlaps retained plus omitted count. No BigTIFF, compression, tiles, SubIFDs, color images, pixel decoding, orientation transforms, GeoTIFF/OME interpretation, metadata cleanup or full baseline TIFF conformance validation. Metadata/metadata aliases are not classified.
brief.acceptance: Both endians, inline/out-of-line arrays, partial strips, exact aliases, metadata collisions, IFD cycles, bad counts/bounds and explicit unsupported format refusal.
brief.notes: Sharp and libvips are broader processing/conversion libraries. Tifffile already exposes data offsets/bytecounts and supports far more TIFF variants. Issue333 about inline ASCII offsets informed careful field storage tests; it is adjacent evidence, not verified demand or a claim that current alternatives lack this capability.
brief.overlap: Owned png-metadata-scrub edits PNG ancillary chunks. This TIFF project reads IFD/strip ownership under a different binary contract and does not edit files.
brief.expected: Exit0: a2x2 invented image has one strip at bytes122..126 with no ownership overlaps.

brief.capability: Prove a bounded minimum-bar plan with explicit between-piece kerf and a search budget.
brief.pain: Greedy allocation can waste a board, while a search cutoff must not be presented as proven optimal.
brief.query: bin packing; cutting stock; official OR-Tools reference follow
brief.contract: Strict JSON stock_length, kerf, pieces. Integer lengths1..1000000, kerf0..1000000;1..24 expanded pieces with unique printable IDs and optional quantity. Unlimited identical stock lengths. Kerf is charged only between adjacent pieces, never at ends. Transform length+kerf into bins of stock+kerf; first-fit decreasing upper bound, valid total-capacity lower bound and exhaustive branch search with equal-free-space symmetry pruning. An optimal claim requires reaching the lower bound or completing search. Oversized pieces return infeasible/exit1; budget exhaustion returns exit2 without a plan or optimality claim.
brief.limits: 64 KiB JSON,250000 search nodes maximum. One stock length, no stock availability/cost objective,2D layouts, end trim, grain, saw sequencing or machine control. The mathematical kerf convention must match the intended planning task; this is not manufacturing certification.
brief.acceptance: Greedy3 versus proven2 counterexample; independent brute-force oracle across small multisets and kerfs; every piece exactly once; conservation, quantities, infeasible inputs and budget refusal.
brief.notes: OR-Tools provides much broader optimization and was found by following its official bin-packing example, not as the top cutting-stock query hit. Opcut is adjacent2D guillotine cutting; csp and stock-cutting are material-planning alternatives. We do not claim faster search, better industrial plans or missing competitor optimality.
brief.overlap: Owned bom-rollup-ledger totals material demand; capacity-cut-report is a network min-cut. Neither solves integer board packing with kerf and an explicit optimality condition.
brief.expected: Exit0: six pieces6,5,3,2,2,2 in stock10 need two bars; the reported first-fit upper bound is three.

brief.capability: Explain small RUP additions with assumptions, unit reasons and an explicit final-empty-clause requirement.
brief.user: SAT experiment authors debugging small unsatisfiability certificates.
brief.pain: A partial or rejected trace needs clause-level reasons; successful intermediate additions do not prove the complete certificate.
brief.query: DRAT proof; DRUP (unrelated Drupal matches excluded)
brief.contract: ASCII DIMACS p cnf header with exact clause count and0 termination;0..64 variables,0..256 initial clauses. Text proof has one addition or d-prefixed deletion per noncomment line. Canonical clauses retain duplicate-clause identities; deletion removes exactly one matching active clause, including units, and absent deletions fail. For each addition assume its negation and perform deterministic unit propagation; report assumptions, implied literals with clause IDs, and conflict. Only an accepted empty clause as the final noncomment step yields verified/exit0. Non-RUP additions and incomplete traces exit1, not a SAT counterexample.
brief.limits: Combined inputs1 MiB,512 steps,2million literal visits. Existing variables only. No RAT, fresh variables, binary DRAT, FRAT or LRAT. Strict unit-deletion application differs from some DRAT-trim modes; no broad compatibility certification. Educational bounded checker, not formally verified or production assurance. Proof comments start with c on their own lines.
brief.acceptance: Clause-reason traces, full/incomplete/rejected proof, contradictory assumptions, initial empty clause, duplicate multiset and unit deletions, final-empty enforcement, DIMACS bounds and visit-budget failure.
brief.notes: DRAT-trim implements much broader DRAT checking and proof output; FRAT carries annotated proof evidence; rate addresses RAT elimination. Their historical research repositories remain useful comparisons even with older push dates. DRAT-trim LRAT issue42/PR43 is a different checker path, not evidence of a defect in RUP or demand for this tool. Existing algorithms are not claimed as new.
brief.overlap: No owned CNF proof checker was found among198 repositories. Numeric and bit-vector tools do not validate clause-addition proofs.
brief.expected: Exit0: addition1 has a unit conflict under assumption-1; the final empty clause is accepted after adding1.
